requirements_summary: Workloads: real-time scoring (low-latency) + end-of-day batch reranking; mixture of chat and reranking calls.
Latency SLOs: p95 <=120ms for scoring model (<=512 tokens), p99 <=250ms target for steady state; batch jobs allowed higher windows.
Throughput: sustained 2.5-3.5k QPS for short-context scoring during peak; burst capacity to 6k QPS for 15-30 minute windows.
Reserved GPU plan: initial commit 4xA100-equivalent VMs (dedicated pool) with autoscale headroom to 8 nodes for peak; planning horizon 12 months.
Model requirements: support for quantized variants (int8) for cost-controls and deterministic fallbacks; KV cache persistence across requests preferred.
Routing/fallback: automatic fallback to lower-capacity quantized model on capacity pressure; route sensitive EU traffic to EU-resident pool.
Security/compliance: SSO/SAML, KMS integration, SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence, audit log retention 1 year, EU residency for specific datasets.
Support: 24/7 on-call, P1 response target disputed (customer requests 15m), dedicated TAM for onboarding.
Maintenance: customer requires a maximal rolling maintenance window of 02:00-06:00 local for EU/NA; 30-day planned-maintenance notice, emergency maintenance only with 2-hour notice and rollback plan.
negotiation_points: Uptime target: customer requests 99.99% — Redwood standard for Dedicated is 99.95%. Discuss tradeoffs, pricing uplift for 99.99 and reduction in credit liability cap.
Credit schedule: customer wants graduated credits starting at <99.99, with larger credit bands. Redwood proposed cap at 20% of monthly fees; customer pushing for 30% for first year.
Maintenance windows: customer requests maintenance outside 06:00-18:00 local and 30-day advance notice; Redwood to propose quarterly maintenance bundles with opt-out for urgent security patches.
Support SLAs: P1 response 15m vs Redwood propose 30m; P2 4 hours; include RTO/RPO for KV cache restoration scenarios.
Reserved GPU lead time: commit to delivery within 6-8 weeks; customer requests guaranteed start date in contract tied to credit if missed.
Data residency clause: explicit guarantee EU-only processing for EU-tagged merchant IDs, with audit rights and third-party attestation deliverables.
Indemnity & liability caps: customer pushing for broader indemnity for data incidents; Redwood counters with industry-standard caps and carve-outs for customer misconfiguration.
reserved_capacity_plan: Initial commitment: 4 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (multi-tenant within customer pool) provisioned in NA and equivalent 2-node pool in EU for EU merchant traffic.
Autoscale policy: baseline 4 nodes, allow burst to 8 nodes for peak windows (end-of-month settlement), burst billing at premium rate.
Throughput/backstop: aim for 3k QPS short-context scoring across pool with p95 latency targets; Redwood to provide perf runbook and capacity testing scripts.
Quantization profile: customer to test int8 model variants for cost savings; Redwood recommended profiling during pilot and mapping latency delta.
Failure tolerance: N+1 within pool for hardware failures; plan to fallback to secondary region with warm replicas if regional outage exceeds 15 minutes.
